thread:
maya.k: heads up — onboarding Borealis-14B. Quick sync: we need weights location, tokenizer quirks, and a short perf matrix (latency/throughput for 1/4/8 batch sizes).
ajenkins: weights are in s3://redwood-models/borealis/14b/v1/ — there was a symlink rename yesterday, use the v1/weights.tar.gz path not `latest/`.
samr: tokenizer note: upstream uses an extra special token `<BOS_cls>` that our tokenizer script drops by default. You might see off-by-one in seq lengths. I converted a test vocab with `python tools/tokenize_fix.py --add-bos` and it fixed alignment.
eva-l: config we intend to use for catalog entry is under repo: `infra/catalog/borealis/14b/config.yaml`. Key flags: `max_input_len: 2048`, `prefetch_kv: true`, `quant_profile: q4_0`. Also confirm `max_batch_tokens` vs `max_batch_size` — new runtime honors tokens.
maya.k: thanks. Can someone run a quick smoke perf on a 512/1024 seq with batch sizes 1,4,8 and share p50/p95 latency + tps? Keep logging verbose so we can see kernel selection. Also want to know memory headroom at peak.
ajenkins: I can run the smoke on dedicated dev pool later today. quick command I'll use:
```
./run_bench --model s3://redwood-models/borealis/14b/v1/weights.tar.gz \n  --tokenizer repo/tokenizers/borealis --seq 1024 --batches 1,4,8 \n  --profile kernels,kv-cache --log-level debug \n  --out /tmp/borealis-smoke.json
```
samr: when you run, add `--tokenizer-fix add_bos` or you'll hit an off-by-one in the attention mask.
perf-bot: scheduled perf job #P-4921 for user `ajenkins` on dev-gpu-pool at 2026-06-17T18:45Z. Logs: https://perf.redwood.internal/jobs/P-4921
ops-bot: dev-gpu-pool quota available: 18/20 GPUs free. Note: nightly cleanup at 02:00 UTC may evict long-running tests.
maya.k: good catch on eviction. Please run with `--ttl 30m` and small warmup. Target regression boundary: p95 should not exceed baseline + 12% for seq512, +20% for seq1024. If exceeded, tag @samr and @eva-l.
ajenkins: starting now (ttl 30m). will paste the short results when done.
samr: small snippet if helpful to post in results: 
```
# convert vocab
python tools/tokenize_fix.py --input repo/tokenizers/borealis/vocab.json --output /tmp/vocab_fixed.json --add_bos
```
eva-l: FYI check `kernel_hint: fp16_cutlass` in config.yaml — runtime may switch to `triton-fused` for longer seqs, which explains p95 jumps we saw earlier.
maya.k: perfect — pinging to follow up on the output. If everything looks clean we'll update catalog entry and schedule canary deploy to hosted later this week. :thumbsup:
ajenkins: results pasted: /tmp/borealis-smoke.json -> brief summary: seq512 p50 42ms p95 86ms tps(1) 23, tps(4) 78, tps(8) 140; seq1024 p50 88ms p95 214ms tps(1) 11, tps(4) 42, tps(8) 70. Memory headroom ~8GB on 80GB GPU. I'll upload full logs to the perf job link.
maya.k: those numbers look within expected for q4_0 but p95 seq1024 is close to the +20% threshold — @samr can you quickly look at the kernel trace and see if the runtime fell back to triton-fused?
samr: checking trace... yes, at ~75% of tokens kernel hint switched to triton-fused for the long kv ops. likely due to `prefetch_kv` + seq1024. Suggest retry with `--kernel-hint cutlass_force` to force cutlass path for comparison.
eva-l: if cutlass reduces p95, we can add a model-specific kernel_hint in catalog to stabilize hosted SLOs.
maya.k: ok aj — can you re-run one seq1024 batch with `--kernel-hint cutlass_force` and attach delta to the same perf job? That should be quick.
ajenkins: running now, ETA ~6m.
maya.k: thanks all — I'll wait for the cutlass numbers then decide canary timing.
